title: Immediate security and compliance truth repair
question: Which security and compliance statements are true of the pinned release?
evidence_ids: AUTH-008;server test suite lacks auth/tenant/audit-integrity suite
competing_evidence: Whitepaper asserts fail-closed RBAC/RLS, tenant isolation, hash-chained audit, and regulated-industry readiness; pinned core parses GRANT without execution and pinned server routes are unauthenticated with mutable SQLite audit rows.
options: A retain assurance|B qualify as reference design and remove readiness/compliance assurance|C remove security design
consequences: Prevents unsafe reliance while preserving future architecture; narrows current positioning.
acceptance_evidence: All current-tense control/readiness claims qualified; absent-control table published; security authority signs boundary; publication review finds no unqualified assurance.
owner: Documentation integration owner; security design authority

title: Lifecycle, freshness, create semantics, and query gating
question: What canonical states and freshness conditions gate create, refresh, preview, and ordinary query?
evidence_ids: Focused core retired-query probe;CS-7;CS-15;CS-18;server catalog/scheduler tests
competing_evidence: Paper has a nine-state FSM and incompatible freshness vocabulary/codes; core creates active and does not gate retired contexts; server rewrites create to draft and exposes four states; specification defines stale_after with W100/W101.
options: A implement nine persisted states|B four durable governance states plus orthogonal runtime status|C informational metadata only
recommendation: B: atomically create draft; only active is ordinarily queryable; preview evaluates pre-active definitions; stale/failed/refreshing follows CS-15; use stale_after.
consequences: Simpler testable safety boundary; breaks callers reading draft/retired contexts; requires core/server atomic create alignment.
acceptance_evidence: Shared transition matrix; restart and invalid-transition tests; query/preview matrix for every state; clock-controlled W100/W101 tests; concurrent refresh and atomic-create tests; docs/OpenAPI gate.
owner: Core semantics owner; server control-plane owner; operations owner consulted

title: Explain execution safety
question: Is server explain side-effect-free or an executing trace endpoint?
competing_evidence: Paper and core imply dry plan; server /query/explain executes, calls providers, and returns rows plus trace.
options: A keep executing explain|B dry explain plus distinct trace endpoint|C required mode in one endpoint
recommendation: B: make explain dry and expose explicitly named, query-authorized, bounded execution trace separately.
consequences: Existing explain-row clients migrate; aligns safety expectations and core/server semantics.
acceptance_evidence: No-execution spies across adapter/provider/DDL/refresh; trace auth and bounds tests; OpenAPI side-effect metadata; compatibility/deprecation test.
owner: Server API owner; security design authority

title: Provider registry activation and health
question: When does persisted provider metadata become routable, and what does healthy mean?
competing_evidence: CRUD stores enabled/health metadata, but startup does not instantiate persisted providers and health returns stored state; built-ins are wired separately.
options: A informational registry|B authoritative activation with desired/observed state|C split registries
recommendation: B: registry-driven allowlisted factory/credential activation, separate desired and observed state, active probes, fail-closed routing, per-provider degraded failure.
consequences: Adds security and operations surface; converts decorative metadata into runtime contract and reveals configuration failures.
acceptance_evidence: API-only configuration survives restart and queries; bad credential/factory/endpoint/timeout/schema/disabled/recovery tests; probe timestamps/reasons; secret-redaction; idempotent activation.
owner: Federation owner; server operations owner; security owner consulted

title: Identity scope and naming
question: Is current functionality deterministic identity binding or canonical confidence-based resolution?
competing_evidence: Accepted design and paper describe global canonical/confidence identity; runtime sync performs exact path-pair binding and ignores resolution metadata.
options: A implement full v1 resolver|B reframe as deterministic identity binding and defer resolution|C remove registry
recommendation: B: retain and accurately name binding; reject inert fields; supersede v1 timing of canonical/confidence resolution.
consequences: May require API migration; prevents governance assumptions; future resolution remains a substantial privacy/security design.
acceptance_evidence: Unambiguous API/docs; every field effective or rejected; cross-key/restart binding tests; future resolver decision includes ambiguity, provenance, privacy, lifecycle, and auth evidence.
owner: Identity/governance owner; federation and security owners consulted

title: API, release, and core/server compatibility identity
question: Which server, HTTP, core, and language versions identify a supported combination?
competing_evidence: Package/README say server 0.1.0, FastAPI/startup say 0.3.0, core is 0.2.0, dependency is a range, routes are unversioned while paper uses /v1.
options: A unversioned HTTP plus package SemVer|B /v1 plus one generated release version and tested pair matrix|C experimental API until stabilization
recommendation: B with time-bounded compatibility alias or explicit breaking release; distinguish server, HTTP-major, core, and language/spec versions.
consequences: Requires route/client migration; enables reproducible diagnostics, audit, compatibility, and deprecation.
acceptance_evidence: One generated version across package/CLI/OpenAPI/health/audit/README/tag; versioned or expressly experimental routes; committed tested pair matrix; OpenAPI diff and deprecation gate.
owner: Release/API compatibility owner; core and server maintainers

title: Ignored context-update fields
question: Are entity_key, has_score, and classification mutable, immutable, or unsupported?
competing_evidence: Request model accepts fields but update service ignores them; successful response can silently fail to apply intent.
options: A implement all mutable|B remove/reject until semantics accepted|C classification mutable and key/score require recreate
recommendation: B now, then decide per field; never succeed on an ignored supplied value. C is likely target only after classification authorization/audit design.
consequences: Strict rejection may break nominally successful clients, but current intent is already not applied; future shape changes require migration/invalidation rules.
acceptance_evidence: Per-field persisted/engine/version/snapshot/audit/restart contract or stable rejection; explicit null distinct from omission; OpenAPI only exposes effective fields.
owner: Catalog API owner; core storage owner; security owner for classification

title: Storage, MVCC, isolation, and performance claim scope
question: Which storage tiers, concurrency guarantees, and performance numbers describe implemented reference behavior?
competing_evidence: Paper claims automatic Roaring/Arrow/Parquet tiers, broad latency/asymptotic performance and MVCC isolation; evidence supports set/Roaring reference storage, one unregenerated benchmark, and SQLite copy-and-promote only.
options: A keep architectural shorthand|B split implementation, measured scenario, and target architecture|C implement complete design first
recommendation: B: say versioned immutable snapshots/copy-and-promote unless query-lifetime isolation is proven; publish only reproducible scoped benchmarks.
consequences: Narrows marketing; preserves architecture as roadmap; EQ-5/EQ-7 need target/superseded status unless scheduled.
acceptance_evidence: Clean benchmark artifacts; concurrent reader/refresh lifetime tests; proof for every tier/movement claim; claim-to-evidence checks; no unsupported asymptotic/platform-wide latency.

title: Generic streaming versus connector synchronization
question: Does v1 ship generic micro-batching/streaming or connector-specific change-feed synchronization?
competing_evidence: OPS-3/paper promise embedded v1 one-second micro-batching while other passages defer streaming; DeepSee has bounded connector-specific ordered/idempotent folding only.
options: A complete generic current roadmap|B supersede v1 commitment and scope docs to connector sync|C immediately extract generic connector SDK
recommendation: B; consider C only after a second connector. Do not label scheduler/watch/polling/one connector as streaming.
consequences: Removes false v1 differentiator; future generic contract must define delivery, ordering, replay, backpressure, schema and recovery.
acceptance_evidence: Scoped terminology; OPS-3 explicitly superseded/deferred; existing connector guarantees retained; future protocol has second implementation plus load/failure evidence and SLOs.

title: Audit integrity and evidentiary scope
question: Is the audit store operational history, append-only control, or tamper-evident compliance evidence?
competing_evidence: Paper promises hash-chained append-only Parquet and reproducibility; server appends mutable SQLite rows by convention without authentication, integrity, retention, or proven complete coverage.
options: A operational log only|B local hash chain|C threat-modeled tamper-evident profile with protected/external anchor
recommendation: A for current release and C before compliance-evidence claims; local self-recomputable chain alone is insufficient.
consequences: Preserves observability but denies independent evidentiary assurance; stronger profile adds keys, schema, operations, migration, privacy and review costs.
acceptance_evidence: Immediate limitation/coverage docs; then threat model, canonical schema, authenticated access, protected checkpoints, mutation/truncation/replay/key-rotation/export tests, retention/privacy review, independent assessment.

title: Server README and control-plane maturity
question: What implemented surface and maturity boundary should the server README publish?
competing_evidence: OpenAPI has 27 routes and durable single-node capabilities omitted from README; auth/versioning/active providers/multi-node/production operations are absent; paper adds unsupported formats/transports.
options: A keep minimal|B document single-node reference surface and explicit limits|C declare all routes stable public API
recommendation: B: generated route inventory plus hand-authored semantics, failure/persistence boundaries and non-capabilities; health wording must match actual fields.
consequences: Improves discoverability without inflating M4/M5 repository evidence to production maturity; experimental/stable status still follows API packet.
acceptance_evidence: README/OpenAPI route match; supported examples/failures; explicit SQLite/single-node/durability/limits/scheduler/backup/migration/auth/provider/identity boundaries; format/transport truth; CI drift check.
